## Facebook Page

The Fed held on October 28. Both dissenters wanted a hike.

The Fed's October 28 hold was a 10-2 decision. Both dissenters wanted higher rates.

Why it matters: Capital Chronicle's reading is that the decision and its implementation answer different questions. The vote establishes the target range and the direction of disagreement. The companion note sets out the rates and instructions used to implement that stance. A reader needs both documents to distinguish the policy choice from its operating settings.

Retrospective analysis, written on 1 November 2026 (GMT+7) Analysis, not financial advice. Readers decide whether to trade.

[What did the majority approve, and in which direction did the dissenters disagree?](file:///A:/Capital%20Chronicle/Worktrees/ContentOps/codex-publisher-backlog/docs/publisher/CC-074-private-20261101/media_assets/cc074-fomc-20261028-vote-direction.png)
*A two-category vote comparison joins the strength of the majority to the direction of dissent. It prevents an undifferentiated split-vote graphic from suggesting the dissenters wanted a cut or that the committee was evenly divided. Name the two dissenters beside their preference; do not invent a majority-member roster. · Source: [Federal Reserve Board](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm)*
[Which announced rates define the target band, and which are settings for separate operating instruments?](file:///A:/Capital%20Chronicle/Worktrees/ContentOps/codex-publisher-backlog/docs/publisher/CC-074-private-20261101/media_assets/cc074-fomc-20261028-rate-framework.png)
*A shared-rate-axis comparison makes the target interval visually distinct from the individual administered settings. It prevents the 3.90 percent reserve-balances rate from being mistaken for the federal funds target or an observed market rate, and it shows that equal numeric settings can belong to different instruments. · Sources: [Federal Reserve Board](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm); [Federal Reserve Board](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a1.htm)*
